Name: Rule30Research
Description: Research provenance and dependency-aware assessments. Human-readable proofs remain imported assertions, not formal certificates.

Assertions.Description: Every claim in the ledger: definitions, theorems, finite verifications, hypotheses and falsified attempts.

schema.name: Kind
schema.Description: Role of the claim in the research: Definition, Theorem, Known result, Finite check, Hypothesis, Bridge obligation or Prize problem.

schema.name: IntroducedInLoop
schema.Description: The Effortless loop that added this claim; empty for claims carried over from research v05.

schema.name: StatusGroup
schema.Description: Proved (definition, proved or rederived known), Checked (finite verification only), Falsified, Superseded or Open.

schema.name: PremiseCount
schema.Description: Direct premises this claim depends on.

schema.name: DependentCount
schema.Description: Claims that list this one as a direct premise.

schema.name: EvidenceCount
schema.Description: Evidence files linked to this claim.

schema.name: RevisionCount
schema.Description: Recorded status changes of this claim.

schema.name: DescendantCount
schema.Description: Claims that rest on this one, directly or transitively.

data.Statement: Single seed, infinite lattice, Rule 30, time starts at zero.
data.Name: D0

data.Statement: Cone support and both boundary cells equal one.
data.Name: T0

data.Statement: Fixed diagonal k has period dividing 2^k.
data.Name: T004

data.Statement: Least antiderivative period is Q or 2Q according to forcing parity.
data.Name: TA

data.Statement: First diagonal one occurs at ceil(k/2); least period exceeds that time.
data.Name: TB

data.Statement: For every T,p a mismatch occurs in column 0 or 1 by t=2T+p.
data.Name: TC

data.Statement: Constant center runs obey the proved endpoint bounds.
data.Name: TD

data.Statement: The center is not eventually constant.
data.Name: K1

data.Statement: Generic n-step output is XOR-affine in its extreme-left input.
data.Name: TE

data.Statement: Time-indexed CMCC equations uniquely reproduce Rule 30.
data.Name: CM

data.Statement: All supplied numerical outputs reproduced.
data.Name: F1

data.Statement: Exact diagonal periods certified through offset 51.
data.Name: F2

data.Statement: 100001 center bits checked twice; periods 1..10000 excluded for onsets through 90000.
data.Name: F3

data.Statement: 33411 SQLite cells match independent evolution.
data.Name: F4

data.Statement: All diagonals k>=1 are balanced over their least period.
data.Name: H1

data.Statement: Periods double at every k>=3.
data.Name: H2

data.Statement: Cone support, first arrival and unbounded diagonal periods imply aperiodic moving diagonal.
data.Name: H3

data.Statement: Least diagonal periods never decrease.
data.Name: H4

data.Statement: ACID alone implies transaction-order independence.
data.Name: H5

data.Statement: Scalar aggregation results may always be nested without preserving group weights.
data.Name: H6

data.Statement: Periodic center of every p>=2 forces a contradiction with seed-compatible neighboring columns.
data.Name: B1

data.Statement: Uniform sublinear center discrepancy bound.
data.Name: B2

data.Statement: Uniform machine-model lower bound with agreed asymptotic quantifiers.
data.Name: B3

data.Statement: The Rule 30 center is not eventually periodic.
data.Name: P1

data.Statement: The center has limiting frequency one-half.
data.Name: P2

data.Statement: The official computational-effort conjecture, once model and quantifiers are fixed.
data.Name: P3

data.Statement: For k>=3 and P=max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}): if q_k(P/2)=1 then the least period of the forcing word q_k=y_{k-1} OR y_{k-2} is exactly P.
data.Name: TF

data.Statement: If j>=1 and eps_j=1 (least period of y_j is twice that of its forcing word) then y_j(P_j/2)=1.
data.Name: TG

data.Statement: For k>=3, if some parent j in {k-1,k-2} attains P=max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}) and has eps_j=1, then Q_k=P.
data.Name: TH

data.Statement: For all k>=3 the least period of the forcing word equals max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}); no OR of two parent diagonals ever has a period smaller than both.
data.Name: H7

data.Statement: If H7 holds for all k>=3 then the least diagonal periods are nondecreasing (H7 implies H4).
data.Name: TI

data.Statement: Exact least diagonal periods, forcing periods and parities certified through offset 64 (largest period 2^27) by an independent big-integer implementation that reproduces all 52 v05 period-word hashes and agrees with a direct lattice evolution for t<=4096.
data.Name: F5

data.Statement: Every diagonal is 1 at its half period: y_j(P_j/2)=1 for all j>=1 (would close the open case of H7 through TF at t=0).
data.Name: H14

data.Statement: Cascade lemma: for k>=4 and P=max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}), if y_j(P/2)=1 for some 2<=j<=k-1 then Q_k=P.
data.Name: TJ

data.Statement: For every k>=3, Q_k=max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}), and the least diagonal periods are nondecreasing (induction on k using TJ, TG, TA).
data.Name: TK

data.Statement: For every k>=3, P_k = P_{k-1}*(1+eps_k): the least period repeats or doubles, never otherwise; and it doubles infinitely often.
data.Name: TL

data.Statement: For k>=4, if eps_{k-1}=1 then eps_k = ones_{k-2} mod 2 (doubling at k decided by the parity of the grandparent diagonal).
data.Name: H15

data.Statement: eps_k = ones_{k-2} mod 2 for every k>=4, with no doubling assumption on k-1.
data.Name: H16

data.Statement: After a doubling at k-1 (k>=4), eps_k equals the parity of the number of ones of y_{k-2} over its least period.
data.Name: TM

data.Statement: For k>=5 the least diagonal period never doubles three times in a row; hence log2 P_k <= log2 P_k0 + ceil(2(k-k0)/3).
data.Name: TN

data.Statement: Finite discrepancy: |2 S(N) - N| <= 3 sqrt(N) for all 16 <= N <= 2^20, S(N) the number of ones among c(0..N-1).
data.Name: H9

data.Statement: Finite run bound: every maximal constant center run [T,V] with 1 <= T and V < 2^20 - 1 has length <= 2 log2(T+1) + 4.
data.Name: H13

data.Statement: For every period 1 <= p <= 2^17 and every onset T <= 917498, some t >= T has c(t) != c(t+p) (2^20 center bits; independent reproduction of E2).
data.Name: F6

data.Statement: Every plateau of the doubling sequence (maximal run of eps_k=0, k>=3) has length at most 7.
data.Name: H18

data.Statement: If every plateau has length at most L, then log2 P_k >= 2 + floor((k-3)/(L+1)) for all k>=3; a plateau bound forces exponential growth of the diagonal periods.
data.Name: TP

data.Statement: Exact diagonal periods certified through offset 72 (largest period 2^31); all 64 E10 period-word hashes reproduced; new diagonals agree with a direct lattice for t<=4096.
data.Name: F7

data.Statement: For k>=3: if eps_k=1 the diagonal has an even number of ones per period; if eps_k=0 that parity equals the parity of the number of ones of q_k at odd positions.
data.Name: TO

data.Statement: eps_k is a function of (eps_{k-1}, eps_{k-2}, o_{k-1}, o_{k-2}) for every k>=5, where o_j is the parity of the number of ones of y_j per period.
data.Name: H19

data.Statement: The center is eventually p-periodic iff some agreement run c(t)=c(t+p) is infinite; so a finite bound on agreement runs for every p implies P1.
data.Name: TQ

data.Statement: On the first 2^20 center bits, every agreement run c(t)=c(t+p) for 1<=p<=4096 has length at most 44.
data.Name: H21

data.Statement: Every left-edge diagonal w_k(t)=x(-t+k,t) is eventually periodic, with least eventual period a power of two dividing 2^k.
data.Name: TR

data.Statement: Exact least eventual periods and onsets of the left-edge diagonals certified for k<=72 (largest period 2^3, latest onset 100); agrees with a direct lattice for t<=4096.
data.Name: F8

data.Statement: The left edge grows at most half as fast as the right: log2(left-edge period of w_k) <= log2(P_k)/2 for every k>=1.
data.Name: H22

data.Statement: Every left-edge diagonal w_k has least eventual period at most 8.
data.Name: H23

data.Statement: Exact left-edge periods and onsets certified for k<=600; reproduces loop 9 for k<=72 and a direct lattice for t<=1600.
data.Name: F9

data.Statement: The left-edge front moves at 5/4: |onset_k/k - 5/4| <= 0.02 for every 1000 <= k <= 5000.
data.Name: H24

data.Statement: Exact left-edge periods and onsets certified for k<=5000; reproduces loop 10 for k<=600 and a direct lattice for t<=1600.
data.Name: F10

data.Statement: Some left-edge diagonal with k < 20000 has least eventual period 32.
data.Name: H25

data.Statement: Exact left-edge periods and onsets certified for k<=19999; for every 20<=k<=19999 the onset exceeds k, so the center c(t)=w_t(t) is read before its left-edge diagonal settles.
data.Name: F11

data.Statement: If the center p-agrees at t and t+1 then column -1 p-agrees at t when c(t)=1, and column -1 p-agrees at t iff column 1 does when c(t)=0: under center agreement, column -1 is column 1 read at the center's zero-times.
data.Name: TS

data.Statement: For every onset 1<=T<=10 and every nonconstant primitive word a of period p<=4, the left cone and the inverse rule alone exclude a p-periodic center of word a from onset T: no column-1 window is compatible once L reaches some L<=4T+4p+8.
data.Name: H26

data.Statement: Left-cone relaxation table for every onset T<=10 and every primitive word of period <=4: the number of column-1 windows (on the zero-times) compatible with a periodic center and the single-seed cone, for L<=4T+4p+8, with the first L that has none; the true (c,r) windows pass the same checker.
data.Name: F12

data.Statement: For every onset T, every p>=2 and every nonconstant word a of least period p, the left-cone relaxation (periodic center word a from T, free column 1, inverse rule, cone of T0) is unsatisfiable at some finite L(T,a).
data.Name: B5

data.Statement: For L>=T the left-cone relaxation is in bijection with rows R at time T on positions -T+1..-1 such that the Rule 30 evolution of the left half from R, with the center prescribed as boundary x(0,t)=c'(t), satisfies x(-1,t)=NOT c'(t+1) at every one-time t<=T+L-1; column 1 is determined, and count(T,a,L)<=2^(T-1).
data.Name: TU

data.Statement: For every primitive nonconstant word a of period p<=6 and every onset 2<=T<=T_max(a) that exact enumeration completes (live-set cap 2^23), the left cone excludes the periodic center with L(T,a)<=4T+4p+8.
data.Name: H27

data.Statement: Exclusion lengths L(T,a) of the left-cone relaxation for every primitive word of period <=6, onsets from 2 up to the enumeration limit per word (largest completed onset 144); vectorised search validated against the loop 13 table and an independent SAT encoding of TU.
data.Name: F13

Dependencies.Description: Declared one-step logical dependencies between assertions.

schema.name: Conclusion
schema.Description: The assertion that depends on the premise.

schema.name: Premise
schema.Description: The assertion the conclusion relies on.

Prerequisites.Description: Transitive closure of Dependencies, one row per (conclusion, ancestor), regenerated by research/loop_tools.py.

schema.name: ConclusionKey
schema.Description: The assessment this transitive premise feeds.

schema.name: Premise
schema.Description: A transitive ancestor of the conclusion (including itself).

schema.name: IsSelf
schema.Description: 1 for the row pairing a claim with itself.

schema.name: IsBlockingAncestor
schema.Description: 1 when this ancestor is not usable and so blocks the conclusion.

Assessments.Description: Compiled status of each assertion given the status of all its ancestors.

schema.name: Statement
schema.Description: The claim being assessed, in words.

schema.name: StatusGroup
schema.Description: Proved, Checked, Falsified, Superseded or Open, from the reported status.

schema.name: SelfUsable
schema.Description: 1 when the claim itself is usable as a premise.

schema.name: SupportCount
schema.Description: Number of evidence files linked to this assertion.

schema.name: EvidenceGap
schema.Description: 1 when a FINITE_VERIFIED claim has no linked evidence file.

schema.name: AncestorBlockedCount
schema.Description: Ancestors (not counting the claim itself) that are not usable.

schema.name: IsAtRisk
schema.Description: 1 when a claim reported as established rests on an ancestor that is open, falsified or superseded. Should always be 0.

schema.name: AncestorCount
schema.Description: Claims this one rests on, directly or transitively.

schema.name: ProjectKey
schema.Description: Dashboard this assessment rolls up to.

data.Name: revision-H1

data.Reason: k=4 and k=5 both have least period 8.
data.Name: revision-H2

data.Reason: The explicit z-array has eventually zero moving diagonal.
data.Name: revision-H3

data.Reason: Serial add-one/double schedules yield 2 and 1 from zero.
data.Name: revision-H5

data.Reason: Unequal group sizes give average-of-averages 5 versus pooled mean 7.5.
data.Name: revision-H6

data.Reason: Checked directly for k<=51 in E1/E8; reduced to H7 by TI. Not a proof: H7 is finite only.
data.Name: revision-H4-1

data.Reason: Re-verified on every offset 3..64 by E10 (independent implementation); 13 new offsets, no counterexample.
data.Name: revision-H7-1

data.Reason: Re-verified on every offset 1..64 by E10; no counterexample.
data.Name: revision-H4-2

data.Reason: y_5 has period 8 and word 00010101; bit 4 is 0. 17 counterexamples through k=64 (E11).
data.Name: revision-H14-1

data.Reason: Proved by TK (induction with the cascade lemma TJ); the finite checks E8/E10 are now corroboration only.
data.Name: revision-H7-2

data.Reason: Follows from H7 by TI, and is also the second half of TK.
data.Name: revision-H4-3

data.Reason: No counterexample on the 25 doubling offsets in 4..64 (E13); then proved as TM.
data.Name: revision-H15-1

data.Reason: k=6: eps_(k-1)=0, ones_(k-2)=4, but eps_k=1. 20 counterexamples in 4..64.
data.Name: revision-H16-1

data.Reason: Max |2S-N|/sqrt(N) = 2.6511 at N=24979; no N in range exceeds 3. Finite statement only; says nothing about the limit (B2, P2).
data.Name: revision-H9-1

data.Reason: 524859 runs checked; longest is 22 at T=731772. Finite statement only; TD remains the proved bound.
data.Name: revision-H13-1

data.Reason: All complete plateaus through k=72 have length <= 7 (longest 7). Finite only; would give log2 P_k >= 2 + floor((k-3)/8) by TP.
data.Name: revision-H18-1

data.Reason: Longest run over all 4096 shifts is 33 (p=1324, t=82603); median of the per-shift maxima 19. Finite only.
data.Name: revision-H21-1

data.Reason: Holds for every k in [9, 72] (and for k=1..8, inspected before stating it). Finite only.
data.Name: revision-H22-1

data.Reason: w_400 has least eventual period 16 (E27).
data.Name: revision-H23-1

data.Reason: k=1000: onset 1275, ratio 1.2750 (E28). 3990 offsets outside the band.
data.Name: revision-H24-1

data.Reason: No left-edge period above 16 for k<=19999; first k per period {'1': 0, '2': 3, '4': 8, '8': 29, '16': 400} (E29).
data.Name: revision-H25-1

data.Reason: All 200 nonconstant cases (T<=10, p<=4) excluded; first_zero_L/T in [1.0, 13.0] (E30). Finite only.
data.Name: revision-H26-1

data.Reason: Derived from B5 and T0 (PROOFS.md §Route L): a least-period-p>=2 center is nonconstant, the true (c,r) satisfies every left-cone constraint, B5 says none can. Compiles BLOCKED until B5 is discharged.
data.Name: revision-B1-1

Loops.Description: Research loops. Only Kind EFFORTLESS + State VERIFIED rows carry build receipts and hashes.

schema.name: StartedAt
schema.Description: ISO time the loop started; recorded from the native loops after effortless-5.

schema.name: FinishedAt
schema.Description: ISO time the loop was verified.

schema.name: ProofsMade
schema.Description: Claims this loop moved to proved.

schema.name: ProjectKey

data.Hypothesis: Supplied numerical outputs are correct
data.Summary: All original scripts rerun; independent indexing. Confirmed; clarify hash and horizon conventions.

data.Name: legacy-2
data.Hypothesis: Every fixed diagonal is balanced
data.Summary: Exact full periods. Falsified at k=5; replace by forcing-parity condition.

data.Name: legacy-3
data.Hypothesis: Period doubles at every k>=3
data.Summary: Exact period recurrence. Falsified at k=5; retain Q and parity separately.

data.Name: legacy-4
data.Hypothesis: Unbounded diagonal periods force aperiodic center
data.Summary: Explicit z-array with cone support and first arrivals. Falsified as an implication; recurrence coupling remains essential.

data.Name: legacy-5
data.Hypothesis: Periodic adjacent columns are compatible with the seed
data.Summary: Inverse rule plus finite cone boundary. Impossible; explicit finite mismatch window proved.

data.Name: legacy-6
data.Hypothesis: A constant center tail might survive the two-column obstruction
data.Summary: One-tail forces a fixed left neighbor; zero-tail forces monotone right neighbor. Excluded for all onsets; identified as known qualitative result.

data.Name: legacy-7
data.Hypothesis: Local periodic spacetime constraints alone refute candidate center periods
data.Summary: Exhaustive pair-word graphs for p<=8. Local periodic solutions exist; seed compatibility cannot be dropped.

data.Name: legacy-8
data.Hypothesis: Input ensemble balance proves time balance
data.Summary: Sensitivity theorem and exact truth tables. Ensemble theorem proved; transfer to the fixed orbit remains unsupported.

data.Name: legacy-9
data.Hypothesis: CMCC and ordinary evolution agree
data.Summary: SQLite lookups/formulas versus independent rows. All 33,411 cells agree; representation theorem proved.

data.Name: legacy-10
data.Hypothesis: ACID / arbitrary aggregation nesting supply additional invariants
data.Summary: Explicit serial-order and unequal-group counterexamples. General implications rejected; narrow their hypotheses.

data.Name: legacy-11
data.Hypothesis: The finite center exclusions persist at a larger horizon
data.Summary: Two implementations through t=100,000. Stronger finite certificates; no infinite-time promotion.

data.Name: legacy-12
data.Hypothesis: Period calculations survive a different implementation
data.Summary: Whole triangular-state orbit replay. See data/period_verification.json.

data.Name: legacy-13
data.Hypothesis: A periodic center word forces its right neighbor eventually periodic (relaxed graph)
data.Summary: All 1,966 primitive words of length <=10. Every nonconstant word admits recurrent branching; the constant-zero argument does not generalize.

data.Hypothesis: H7: Q_k = max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}) for all k>=3; TF/TG/TH/TI provable; H4 reduces to H7.
data.Summary: Added TF, TG, TH, TI (proved) and H7 (finite through k=51). H4 OPEN->FINITE_VERIFIED with new dependency edges H4<-TI, H4<-H7; TH covers 33 of 49 offsets, the remaining 16 plateau-fed offsets are the open case of H7.
data.Name: effortless-1

data.Hypothesis: F5: exact diagonal periods are certifiable far past k=51; H7 and H4 survive out-of-sample offsets.
data.Summary: Added F5 (frontier k<=64, 2.3s). H7 and H4 re-verified through 64. E1 hashes reproduced: 51/52. Lattice cross-check t<=4096: ok.
data.Name: effortless-2

data.Hypothesis: H14: y_j(P_j/2)=1 for all j (closes the plateau case of H7 at t=0).
data.Summary: H14 falsified at k=5. Added TJ (cascade lemma), TK (H7 and H4 proved by induction), TL (repeat-or-double). H7 and H4 FINITE_VERIFIED->PROVED_HUMAN_READABLE; 19 plateau-fed offsets through 64 are now covered by proof, not data.
data.Name: effortless-3

data.Hypothesis: H15: after a doubling at k-1, eps_k = ones_{k-2} mod 2 (and H16: the same without the doubling).
data.Summary: H15 tested on 25 offsets then proved as TM; H16 falsified at k=6; TN (no triple doubling) proved, giving log2 P_k <= log2 P_k0 + ceil(2(k-k0)/3). Longest observed plateau 7.
data.Name: effortless-4

data.Hypothesis: H9 and H13 hold on the first 2^20 center bits; the onset/period exclusion F3 extends to p <= 2^17.
data.Summary: Center column to 2^20: E2 hash reproduced; F6 excludes all periods <= 2^17 for onsets <= 917498 (F3 was 10^4 / 9*10^4). H9 (max ratio 2.6511) and H13 (longest run 22) finite-verified. P1, P2 unchanged.
data.Name: effortless-5
